questions.prompt: What is a mixture?
questions.answer: Substances mixed together but not chemically bonded
wrong: One substance that can't be separated
questions.explain: In a mixture, like salad dressing, the parts are combined but each keeps being itself.

questions.prompt: A solution is another name for what?
questions.explain: A solution is mixed evenly all the way through, so you can't see its separate parts.

questions.prompt: In salt water, what is the salt called?
questions.explain: The solute is the substance that gets dissolved.

questions.prompt: In sugar water, what is the water called?
questions.explain: The solvent is the substance that does the dissolving. Water is the most common solvent.

questions.prompt: What is a fluid?
questions.answer: Anything that can flow, like a liquid or a gas
wrong: Only things that are very hot
questions.explain: Water, air and oil are all fluids because they can flow.

questions.prompt: What is solubility?
questions.answer: How well a substance dissolves in another
wrong: How hot a substance can get
questions.explain: Something with high solubility dissolves easily, like sugar in water.

questions.prompt: What does the concentration of a solution tell you?
questions.answer: How much solute is in it
questions.explain: A concentrated solution has a lot of solute. A diluted one has only a little.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.explain: In a heterogeneous mixture you can see different parts, and each spoonful is a little different.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a homogeneous mixture?
questions.explain: Dissolved salt spreads evenly through the water, so every drop is the same.

questions.prompt: Water stays H2O whether it is ice, liquid water or steam. This makes water a...
questions.explain: A pure substance has the same makeup no matter what physical changes it goes through.

questions.prompt: Most solid solutes, like sugar, dissolve more easily in water that is...
questions.explain: That's why sugar dissolves faster in hot tea than in iced tea.

questions.prompt: What is pressure?
questions.answer: How much force pushes on an area
wrong: How much matter is in an object
questions.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area. Air inside a balloon pushes outward with pressure.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a unit of pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa) or atmospheres (atm).

questions.prompt: A juice drink tastes watery because it has very little juice in it. It is...
questions.explain: Diluted means there is only a small amount of solute compared to the solvent.

questions.prompt: How does water pressure change as a diver swims deeper?
questions.explain: The deeper you go, the more water is above you pushing down.

questions.prompt: Why does soda stay fizzy longer when it is kept cold?
questions.answer: Gases dissolve better in cold liquids
wrong: Gases dissolve better in hot liquids
questions.explain: Gas solutes are the opposite of solid ones. They stay dissolved better at colder temperatures.

questions.prompt: A force of 20 N pushes on an area of 4 m². What is the pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area, so 20 N ÷ 4 m² = 5 Pa.

questions.prompt: If you push with the same force over a bigger area, what happens to the pressure?
questions.explain: The force is spread over more space, so each part gets less push.

questions.prompt: Why do wide snowshoes keep you from sinking into deep snow?
questions.answer: They spread your weight over a larger area
wrong: They melt the snow under you
They push harder on the snow
questions.explain: A larger area means less pressure on the snow, so you stay on top.

questions.prompt: Why is air pressure lower on top of a tall mountain?
questions.answer: There is less air above pushing down
wrong: The mountain is closer to the Sun
Gravity is much stronger up high
questions.explain: Air pressure comes from the weight of air above you. Up high, there's less air above.

questions.prompt: Why does water boil at a lower temperature high in the mountains?
questions.answer: Lower air pressure lets molecules escape easily
wrong: The air is warmer up high
questions.explain: With less air pressing down, water molecules can break free into gas at a lower temperature.

questions.prompt: A drink is 10% juice. How much juice is in 100 mL of the drink?
questions.explain: 10% means 10 out of every 100 parts, so 100 mL of drink has 10 mL of juice.
